title: Koko Eating Bananas
statement:
Koko loves to eat bananas. There are `n` piles of bananas, the `i`-th pile has `piles[i]` bananas. The guards have gone and will come back in `h` hours.

Koko can decide her bananas-per-hour eating speed of `k`. Each hour, she chooses some pile and eats `k` bananas from it. If the pile has fewer than `k` bananas, she eats all of them instead and does not eat any more that hour.

Return the minimum integer `k` such that she can eat all the bananas within `h` hours.

If speed `k` is enough to finish in time, any speed greater than `k` also works — this monotonicity is what makes binary search on the answer possible: binary search over candidate speeds from 1 to max(piles).

editorial.approach: Binary search over candidate eating speeds from 1 to `max(piles)`. For a given speed `k`, compute the total hours needed as the sum of `Math.ceil(pile / k)` for every pile. If the total hours is at most `h`, speed `k` works, so try a smaller speed (search left half); otherwise search the right half for a faster speed. The smallest feasible speed found is the answer.
